hints.title: Turn the probability into a ratio
hints.body: Equal chances of selection mean that glasses wearersclass size=415. The remaining fraction is 1115, so glasses wearers and non-wearers occur in the ratio 4:11.
hints.recap: A reduced probability fixes a ratio, not one particular group size.
hints.pitfall: The denominator 15 need not be the actual class size.
hints.pause: Write two different integer class compositions with this ratio.

recall.reminder: With equally likely outcomes, probability is the favourable count divided by the full count.

hints.title: Use different allowed class sizes
hints.body: A class with 4 glasses wearers and 11 non-wearers has the required probability. So does a class with 8 glasses wearers and 22 non-wearers.
hints.recap: A necessary condition must hold in every allowed example.
hints.pitfall: An example that works proves possibility; it does not make its exact numbers necessary.
hints.pause: Use these two classes to test statements I and III separately.

recall.reminder: A necessary condition must hold in every allowed example.

hints.title: Describe every possible scale
hints.body: Let the two counts be positive integer multiples of the reduced ratio. Add them to express the general class size.
hints.recap: A necessary divisibility condition must hold for every permitted integer scale.
hints.pitfall: A particular class size cannot establish what every class must satisfy.
hints.pause: Use the general total to assess II, and combine this with your tests of I and III.

recall.reminder: A necessary divisibility condition must hold for every permitted integer scale.

solution:
1. Express every possible class. The fraction 415 is reduced, so glasses/non-glasses counts must be 4k and 11k, with positive integer k. The class size is 15k.

2. Test necessity. Statement I fails when k=2: there are 22 students without glasses. Statement III fails when k=1: the class has 15 students and 4 wear glasses.

3. Prove the remaining condition. The total is 15k=3(5k), so it is always divisible by 3. Only II is necessary: answer C.
knowledgePattern: Infer divisibility from a reduced sampling probability
